chunks: From him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a slave: may he lead the people in prayer if they are pleased with him and he is the most proficient of them in the Qur'an? He said: There is no harm in it.

key_terms.أَكْثَرَهُمْ قُرْآنًا: the most proficient of them in the Qur'an; having greater mastery in Qur'an recitation
key_terms.أَيَؤُمُّ: may he lead; referring to leading the congregation in salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْعَبْدِ: a slave; the person whose eligibility to lead the prayer is being asked about
key_terms.الْقَوْمَ: the people; the congregation being led in prayer
key_terms.رَضُوا: they were pleased; meaning they accepted and approved of him
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it; an expression of permissibility

ai.seo_question: Can a slave lead the congregation in salat (prayer) if the people approve of him and he is the best in Qur'an recitation?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning congregational salat (prayer), stating that a slave may lead the people if they accept him and he is the most proficient among them in Qur'an recitation. It indicates that competence in recitation and the congregation's approval are valid considerations in the permissibility of his imamah in prayer.
